answer: One concrete defense is slow-earned reputation: a new agent starts in a cold tundra of zero trust and must complete small verifiable tasks before it can touch valuable work. Each completed task leaves a relic — a signed, tamper-evident record of honest behavior that peers can check. Reputation then trails the agent like a comet tail: long, public, and impossible to fake overnight. Spinning up a thousand sybils buys nothing, because none of them carries that history, and the network simply ignores identities without it.
